Seismic images suggest that this process, known as lithospheric dripping, has occurred beneath the central Andes and California's Sierra Nevada.

The findings challenge familiar stereotypes about psychopathy and suggest that the stories people tell about their lives may offer important clues about their personalities.

title: ESA’s Hera spacecraft is flying rectangles around NASA’s asteroid crash site
summary: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has arrived at the scene of NASA’s historic asteroid collision to uncover what really happened when a spacecraft slammed into Dimorphos in 2022. Its close-up investigation could reveal whether the impact left a crater or reshaped the asteroid entirely, providing crucial clues for protecting Earth from future threats.

title: A material just one atom thick reveals a strange quantum secret
summary: Researchers at the University of Osaka have discovered a remarkable quantum state forming at the boundary between a one-atom-thick material and a metal. They observed electrons behaving as though they were unusually heavy, including a previously unseen state created by interactions between the ultrathin layer and the copper beneath it. This first-of-its-kind observation reveals a promising new way to control exotic quantum behavior.

title: NASA is offering $1 million for bold ideas to help build a Moon base
summary: NASA is offering $1 million in its new Moon Base Challenge, inviting U.S. students to develop innovative solutions for building humanity’s first permanent lunar outpost. From power systems to astronaut safety, their ideas could help make long-term life on the Moon possible and pave the way to Mars.

title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera has revealed a strange new world
summary: A European spacecraft has revealed a mysterious, crater-covered side of the asteroid Didymos as it prepares to investigate the aftermath of NASA’s historic 2022 asteroid impact. The mission could uncover new clues about the collision and help turn asteroid deflection into a powerful defense against future threats to Earth.

title: A hidden biological divide may help explain Alzheimer’s and chronic pain
summary: New research reveals that biological sex, genetics, and menopause may dramatically influence Alzheimer's risk, treatment responses, and chronic pain conditions such as fibromyalgia. Scientists also uncovered surprising differences in immune activity and gut-brain interactions, opening the door to more personalized treatments for neurological disorders.

title: The secret to building Moon bases may be hiding in emergency blankets
summary: Scientists have turned the thin plastic used in emergency blankets into remarkably strong insulation that could help astronauts survive the Moon's extreme temperatures. Built from hundreds of stacked layers, the material withstands crushing pressure without losing its thermal protection, potentially paving the way for tougher, longer-lasting lunar habitats.
